chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad reported to me from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja’far al-Himyari, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas’adah ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, and he was asked about the saying of the Most High:

“To Allah belongs the conclusive argument,” so he said: Surely, Allah, Most High, will say to the servant on the Day of Resurrection: ‘O My servant, were you learned?’ If he says: ‘Yes,’ He will say to him: ‘Did you not act upon what you knew?’ And if he says: ‘I was ignorant,’ He will say to him: ‘Did you not seek knowledge so that you could act?’ Thus He will defeat him in argument, and that is the conclusive argument.
And may Allah bless our master and our Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet, and his progeny, and grant them abundant peace.

key_terms.الحجة البالغة: The conclusive argument; Allah's irrefutable proof against His servants
key_terms.جاهل: Ignorant; one lacking knowledge, with the implication that this state is not excusable
key_terms.فيخصمه: He defeats him in argument; Allah silences all excuses

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'To Allah belongs the conclusive argument' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of al-Mufid, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) explains the Quranic verse 'To Allah belongs the conclusive argument' (6:149). He describes how on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will question each person: if they were learned, why they did not act on their knowledge; if they were ignorant, why they did not seek knowledge to act upon. This dialogue represents Allah's irrefutable proof against His servants, establishing that both knowledge and action are obligatory, and neither ignorance nor inaction can serve as valid excuses.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad reported to me from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja’far al-Himyari, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas’adah ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, say when he was asked about the verse in Qu’ran: ’To Allah belongs the conclusive authority’ [6:149], he said:

"Surely, Allah, Most High, will ask His slave on the Day of Reckoning: ’O my slave, were you learned?’ If he said: ’Yes,’ Allah would say: ’Did you not act according to your knowledge?’ And if he said: ’I was unlearned, ignorant’; Allah would say: ’Did you not acquire knowledge so that you could act accordingly?’ That will be the time of His argument against him and that is the conclusive authority."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his progeny.
